title: Which is larger, six point four five six or six point four six five?
description: Two decimals are compared place by place from the left, and we ask why we can stop at the first difference. Keeko doubts the result and thinks 6.456 is larger.
teaching_notes: One idea: compare from the left, and the first place where the digits differ decides. Watch for students who compare the last digits or the whole digit strings.

source: Which is larger, 6.456 or 6.465? Compare step by step and sa
video_script.why: The child can read and place decimals on a line and now compares two of them using place value.
video_script.substitution: Compare digit by digit from the left, and stop at the first place where the digits differ.
video_script.anchor: the two decimals 6.456 and 6.465 in the book, with the step by step comparison
video_script.wrong_answer: six point four five six is larger
video_script.wrong_move: Says 6.456 is larger without comparing place by place from the left.
video_script.payoff_line: The first place where the digits differ decides

final_answer.spoken: six point four six five is larger

video_script.design: The two decimals stand one above the other with their digits in columns. Each column lights up in turn from the left, and the deciding column keeps its colour.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; 6.456 above 6.465 in digit columns

marks.ask: the two decimals appear in columns
marks.stop: a stop sign appears at the hundredths column

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about comparing decimals.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Which is larger, six point four five six or six point four six five?
<bookmark mark='stop'/>And why can we stop comparing at some place?

beats.on_screen: the two decimals stay on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits beside the two decimals

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: highest place first: units, tenths, hundredths, thousandths

marks.order: the places are listed from the highest to the lowest
marks.left: an arrow runs from left to right along the digits

narration: <bookmark mark='order'/>The digit with the highest place value counts for the most.
<bookmark mark='left'/>We start at the left, and move right one place at a time.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the decimals six point four five six, and six point four six five.

beats.on_screen: To find: the larger decimal; why we can stop
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the larger decimal.
<bookmark mark='find2'/>We also say why we can stop comparing.

beats.on_screen: units: 6 and 6, equal; tenths: 4 and 4, equal

marks.u: the units column lights up and the two sixes match
marks.t: the tenths column lights up and the two fours match

narration: <bookmark mark='u'/>Step one, compare the units. Both have six, so they are equal.
<bookmark mark='t'/>Compare the tenths. Both have four, so they are equal again.

marks.h: the hundredths column lights up and the digits differ

narration: <bookmark mark='h'/>Step two, compare the hundredths. The digits are five and six.
<bookmark mark='gt'/>Six is greater than five, so six point four six five is the greater number.

marks.rest: the digits after the hundredths are split off
marks.less: zero point zero zero six is shown smaller than one hundredth

narration: <bookmark mark='rest'/>Step three, why can we stop? The first number is six point four five plus zero point zero zero six.
<bookmark mark='less'/>The digits after the hundredths are always worth less than one hundredth.
That keeps the first number below six point four six.

marks.chain: the chain of three numbers is written
marks.done: the later digits are crossed out as not needed

narration: <bookmark mark='chain'/>Step four, the second number is already at least six point four six.
<bookmark mark='done'/>The later digits cannot change the answer, and we can stop.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The first place where the digits differ decides.
Six point four six five is larger.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the two decimals
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: a speech bubble: 6.456 is larger; the digits match until the hundredths; the bubble is crossed out

marks.fix: the matching columns glow, then the hundredths column glows alone

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks six point four five six is larger, since it ends with a six.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But the digits are all the same until the hundredths place.
<bookmark mark='decide'/>The first place where they differ decides, and there five is less than six.
